note: Procedure parent; its steps are classified individually.

outcome: Only untapped non-battle creatures that have haste or were controlled since the turn began are legal attackers.
A creature affected by a can't-attack restriction, or whose attack condition is unmet, is not a legal attacker.
A creature that must attack if able is required in the declaration, up to the maximum number of requirements satisfiable without breaking restrictions.
Each declared attacker becomes tapped unless it has vigilance, and this is not a cost.

note: Total cost determination and lock-in; the observable payment is the attack cost's effect.

outcome: Each chosen creature still controlled by the active player becomes an attacking creature and appears among the attackers of the combat.
Abilities that trigger on attackers being declared fire when the attackers are declared.

note: Priority is given after the declaration; handled by 117.

outcome: An attack trigger fires only on declaration, not when an attacking creature later changes to match the condition.
Abilities triggered by the declaration are put on the stack before the active player receives priority.

note: Introduces the variety of attack trigger conditions; the subrules carry the outcomes.

outcome: Whenever-creature-attacks triggers fire for a declared attacker (and the named defender) but not for a creature put onto the battlefield attacking.
Whenever-player-or-permanent-is-attacked triggers fire when creatures are declared attacking it, not when one enters attacking.
Whenever-player-attacks-with-a-creature triggers fire for a declared attacker that player controls.
Whenever-player-attacks triggers fire once if one or more of that player's creatures are declared as attackers.
Whenever-player-attacks-another-player triggers fire for declared attackers attacking that player, not for creatures entering attacking or attacking planeswalkers or battles.
Attacks-and-isn't-blocked triggers fire in the declare blockers step, not at declaration.
A creature put onto the battlefield attacking is an attacking creature that never attacked, so declaration triggers do not fire for it.
note: Choice of defender is a decision; the never-attacked consequence is observable.

outcome: A creature that would enter attacking a player or permanent that is gone or no longer a valid defender enters the battlefield but is not attacking.
An effect that makes a creature attack a specific defender does nothing to it if that defender is no longer valid when the effect resolves.
A creature put onto the battlefield attacking ignores attack requirements and restrictions.
A creature put onto the battlefield attacking after blockers are declared is unblocked and stays unblocked until it is removed from combat, becomes blocked by an effect, or combat ends.

A reference to the defending player resolves to the player attacked, the controller of the attacked planeswalker, or the protector of the attacked battle, including after the creature is removed from combat.

note: Defines the phrases attacking a player and has attacked a player; their consequences are covered by trigger and condition rules.
Introduces reselection of the attacked defender; subrules carry the outcomes.

outcome: A reselected attacker stays in combat, is not treated as having attacked again, and attacks the new defender while still counting as having attacked the original one.
A creature whose defender is reselected is not subject to attack requirements or restrictions.
A reselected defender must be an opponent, a planeswalker an opponent controls, or a battle an opponent protects.

note: Multiplayer limited range of influence rule.

outcome: If no creatures are declared as attackers or put onto the battlefield attacking, the declare blockers and combat damage steps are skipped.
